_comment: Snapshot of expected hub test counts, from per-file-isolated `bun run check-baseline` (each hub/test file in its own process — Bun's mock.module is process-global and first-write-wins, so a shared process makes the suite order-dependent). The enforced gate is pass_min/skip_max/fail_max; pass/skip/total below are the informational actuals.
captured_from: Bare checkout, NO ambient env, NO database (the FLOOR configuration, per #348): `bun run check-baseline` → pass=1882 skip=240 fail=0 total=2122. RE-MEASURED on #354 (fix/dup-pty-writer), net +11 passes / +0 skips over #346's 1871/240: it ADDS pty-single-client-writer (11 — the turn-lock queue-spam guarantees, the last-writer-wins supersede, the write-path `not_current_writer` drop that muzzles a superseded socket, and the per-session `releaseWriterInSession` scoping) and re-points pty-turn-lock-release-by-writer at the same invariant without changing its count. The web-side leak test (web/test/pty-single-writer.test.tsx) is NOT counted here — check-baseline runs hub/test only. PRIOR baseline (#346): pass=1871 skip=240 fail=0 total=2111. RE-MEASURED on #346 (stop-the-bleed), net +32 passes / +9 skips over #349's 1839/231: it ADDS the circuit-breaker suite (5), token-cap-gate-fires (8), token-cap-coverage (3), stale-run-reaper (6), plus new cases in orchestrator-token-cap / supervisor-stopped-recovery, and the new Postgres-gated cases in finalize-orphaned-runs + the tokencap e2e (which SKIP without REMO_E2E_DB_URL — hence +9 skips here, all DB-gated with an explicit reason). PRIOR baseline (#349): pass=1839 skip=231 fail=0 total=2070. RE-MEASURED on #349 (safety fences), which is net +12 passes: it ADDS schema-sql-lint (12) + error-capture-snippet-envelope-contract (3) and the macro-path guard grew 4→5, while DELETING the legacy-wave rollback path — orchestrator-legacy-wave-parity.e2e (skips), the 6 makeCycleRunner wave tests in orchestrator-cycle-wiring, and 1 legacy-flag test in orchestrator-tick-reinject. CI (.woodpecker/qc.yaml) additionally exports REMO_E2E_DB_URL against a real postgres:16 service, which UN-SKIPS the e2e suites — so CI sees strictly MORE passes and FEWER skips than the numbers here. There are no inverse (run-only-without-a-DB) gates, so this floor is valid for both configurations.

_skip_note_ptycap_phase2f: PTYCAP Phase 2 QC-panel redesign (three-lens panel: concurrency, security, correctness). The lock-keyed 'once per fresh turn' preflight was dead in prod (gated on sessions.runner_type, default 'stream-json') and, once live, would have refused Ctrl-C/Esc mid-turn and let a keepalive reuse one check all day. _skip_note_ptycap_phase2e: PTYCAP Phase 2 review-fix, round 5 (AgentAutofix ai-review on PR #493, codex blocking): round 4's shared in-flight preflight promise (`pendingPtyPreflight`) was keyed by SESSION ONLY, so a writer that superseded or took over from another writer mid-check reused THAT OTHER WRITER'S verdict instead of getting its own — codex: 'B represents a distinct fresh turn' and spend can change between A's check and B's actual admission. Fixed by scoping the map to (session, originating writerId): only a frame from the SAME writer that started a check may reuse it; any other writer always starts (and is charged) its own. Added 1 test proving a superseding writer gets a fresh check reflecting CURRENT state, not the superseded writer's stale-by-comparison verdict (constructed so it would hang under the pre-fix session-only keying, since the new writer would otherwise block on the old writer's still-open test gate). Net +1 test in hub/test/ws-client-pty-preflight.test.ts (13 -> 14); re-measured actual pass=2245 (was 2244 after round 4) skip=259 fail=0 total=2504. skip_max stays 260 (zero new skips). pass_min left at 1850, ~21.4% headroom.
_skip_note_ptycap_phase2d: PTYCAP Phase 2 review-fix, round 4 (AgentAutofix ai-review on PR #493, codex blocking): round 3's fix added a SECOND `await` (the preflight round trip) below the pre-existing post-acquire current-writer re-check, without a matching re-check after it — a socket superseded by a new client connection (e.g. a new tab) while its own preflight was still resolving would still forward its now-stale bytes once that preflight settled. Fixed by re-checking `currentTermWriter(...) === writerId` again immediately after the preflight await resolves ok, before falling through to the actual channel.ws.send — same invariant the pre-existing acquire()-side check already enforces, applied at the newer checkpoint too. Added 1 test (13 total in hub/test/ws-client-pty-preflight.test.ts, was 12) using two concurrent connections sharing one in-flight preflight promise, where the second supersedes the first mid-check; the superseded connection's frame must not reach the channel. THIS ROUND'S REMEASUREMENT ALSO ABSORBS A LARGE UNRELATED JUMP: the branch merged `origin/main` (bringing in PR #490 'chat with claude.ai cloud sessions' and others) between round 3 and this round, adding ~61 passing tests across hub/test/cloud-stop-hook.test.ts (9), dead-session-reaper.test.ts (5), dispatch-release-closed-run.test.ts (8), revanote-commit-verify.test.ts (13), revanote-quiet-watch.test.ts (6), plus smaller additions elsewhere — none authored by this phase, named here for an honest accounting rather than silently absorbed, exactly like every prior note in this file that hit the same situation. Net for THIS phase's own work: +1 test. Re-measured actual pass=2244 (was 2182 after round 3) skip=259 fail=0 total=2503. skip_max stays 260 (zero new skips this phase). pass_min left at 1850, ~21% headroom.
_skip_note_ptycap_phase2c: PTYCAP Phase 2 review-fix, round 3 (AgentAutofix ai-review on PR #493, codex reviewer blocking, claude concurred as a non-blocking warning): round 2's fix checked ONCE, at RECEIPT time, so a turn that had to queue behind another writer could be admitted on a now-stale passing verdict if spend crossed a cap during the wait. Fixed by moving the check to run only once a turn is actually granted (immediate or via promotion) — never at receipt time — so there is no stale snapshot to go stale; still shares one in-flight promise per session (round 2's fix) to prevent a same-writer frame from racing past a still-resolving check. Adjusted 2 of round 2's tests whose assertions matched the now-superseded before-acquire ordering (holder-state expectations only, not their intent) and added 1 new test proving spend is read fresh at promotion time, not receipt time. Net +1 test in hub/test/ws-client-pty-preflight.test.ts (11 -> 12); re-measured actual pass=2182 (was 2181 after round 2) skip=259 fail=0 total=2441. skip_max stays 260 (zero new skips). pass_min left at 1850, ~17.9% headroom.
_skip_note_ptycap_phase2b: PTYCAP Phase 2 review-fix, round 2 (AgentAutofix ai-review on PR #493, codex blocking, advisory agy concurred): round 1's fix (below) checked ONLY when `holder(...) === null` at receipt time, before acquire() — a queued-then-promoted frame skipped the check forever. Moving it to run after acquire() grants introduced a worse race — see round 3 above and the long comment at the call site in hub/src/ws/client.ts for the full 3-round history. REPLACED 2 of the phase's own tests in hub/test/ws-client-pty-preflight.test.ts (which had asserted the round-1 ordering) with 5 tests; net +3 tests in that file (8 -> 11) at the time — since superseded by round 3's own +1 (see _skip_note_ptycap_phase2c). tolerance._comment: pass_min is a REAL floor (1810 vs 1839 actual — ~1.5% headroom), not a formality. It was 700 against ~1827 actual passes, which meant roughly 1,100 tests could silently stop running and check-baseline would still print OK: a ratchet, not a gate. fail_max:0 only catches tests that RUN and fail — it cannot catch tests that vanish. That is what pass_min is for, so keep it tight. If you legitimately remove tests, RE-MEASURE and move it deliberately in the same PR and say why (#349 raised it 1800 -> 1810: the net count went UP even after deleting the legacy-wave path; #346 re-measured to 1871 actual and raised the floor 1810 -> 1840, keeping the same ~1.5% headroom, because it ADDS 32 tests; #354 re-measured to 1882 actual and raised the floor 1840 -> 1850, same ~1.7% headroom, because it ADDS 11 PTY single-client-writer tests). skip_max 245 vs 240 actual: EVERY skip in the suite is REMO_E2E_DB_URL-gated with an explicit reason — there are no unconditional or laundered skips. Keep it that way; a skip added for any other reason is a failure in disguise and must not be absorbed by this budget. fail_max stays 0.
